title: Mathematicians want proof OpenAI didn’t use their work
slides: Did OpenAI train on mathematicians' unpublished proofs?
Their copyrighted papers were submitted for AI training
OpenAI claims fair use, but data provenance is murky
Your research could be in a model without consent
Check if your work is in AI training sets
thread_text:
1. The Unpublished Proofs

OpenAI reportedly trained on mathematicians' papers that were never made public. The data came from peer review servers, not the open web.

2. Caught in the Pipeline

Researchers submitted their work for review, not for training. Those files ended up in AI datasets anyway.

3. Fair Use or Free Ride?

OpenAI says training is fair use, but can't say exactly where the data came from. Provenance is a black box.

4. Your Work, No Permission

If you've ever submitted a paper for review, it may already be inside a model you use daily.

5. Check Your Data

Search your name in AI training set indexes like Have I Been Trained. If you find your paper, you decide what to do next.

instagram.caption:
Mathematicians are demanding proof that OpenAI didn't train on their unpublished proofs.

Their papers were never public. They were sitting on peer review servers, submitted for review only, and somehow ended up in AI training data. 😳

OpenAI calls it fair use but can't say where the data actually came from.

So if you've ever submitted a paper for review, your unpublished work may already be inside a model you use every day. 🔒

Search your name on Have I Been Trained and see what shows up. 🕵️

If you find your paper there, what will you do about it?
